If you’re looking for grants specifically for women-owned businesses, there are actually quite a few options right now, especially if you’re in entity["state","Tennessee","Tennessee, USA"] and running a service-based business like marketing, consulting, wellness, beauty, or education.

Here are the best places to start:

### Best Grants for Women-Owned Businesses

#### urlAmber Grant for Womenhttps://ambergrantsforwomen.com/get-an-amber-grant/
Probably the easiest and most realistic to apply for quickly.

- Monthly $10,000 grants
- Year-end $25K-$50K grants
- Specifically for women entrepreneurs
- Simple application process
- Great for service businesses and newer companies

This is one of the most legitimate and active women-focused grant programs right now. citeturn0search2turn0search8turn0news21

---

#### urlIFundWomen Grants Databasehttps://ifundwomen.com/grants
Excellent for female founders.

- Corporate-sponsored grants
- Minority/women founder opportunities
- Often includes coaching + networking
- New grants added constantly

Good if you want ongoing opportunities instead of one-time applications.

---

#### urlGrants.govhttps://www.grants.gov
This is the federal database.

Important note:
Most federal grants are NOT for general startup money. They are usually for:
- Innovation
- Research
- Technology
- Community programs
- Workforce initiatives

Still worth creating an account because women-owned certifications can help eligibility. citeturn0search1turn0news21

---

#### urlSBA Women-Owned Small Business Programhttps://www.sba.gov/federal-contracting/contracting-assistance-programs/women-owned-small-business-federal-contract-program
Not a grant directly, but VERY valuable.

Benefits include:
- Government contract access
- Certification advantages
- Funding resources
- Business training

This can help long-term if you want larger contracts or partnerships.

---

#### urlTennessee Grant & Funding Resourceshttps://www.tn.gov/rural/search-for-grants---resources.html
Tennessee has rotating state and regional funding programs. citeturn0search7turn0search14

Especially look for:
- Rural business grants
- Workforce grants
- Economic development programs
- Technology and innovation funding

---

### Grants You’d Likely Be Competitive For

Based on your background in:
- marketing/consulting
- women-led business
- workforce/economic development
- med spa and wellness education
- AI/business systems

You’d probably have the strongest chance with:
1. Amber Grant
2. IFundWomen
3. Local Nashville entrepreneur grants
4. Women-in-business pitch competitions
5. Economic development or innovation grants

You are less likely to qualify for:
- pure tech R&D grants
- agriculture/manufacturing grants
- nonprofit-only grants

---

### Biggest Mistake People Make Applying
Most people apply with:
- vague ideas
- emotional stories only
- no measurable outcome

The strongest applications usually explain:
- what the business does
- who it helps
- how funding creates jobs/revenue/community impact
- exactly where the money goes
- why NOW matters

For example, with urlThe Luxora Collectivehttps://theluxoracollective.co, you could position:
- women-led leadership
- supporting women-owned med spas
- workforce education
- AI/business modernization
- helping small aesthetic practices grow sustainably

That angle is actually pretty grant-friendly.

If you want, I can also help you with:
- grants specifically for Tennessee women founders
- minority/women-owned certifications
- emergency hardship grants
- grants for marketing agencies
- grants for wellness/beauty businesses
- a master grant application template you can reuse everywhere
- a list of grants currently open this month only
- help writing a winning application narrative for Luxora/New Era Intel style businesses

supporting_websites.snippet: Nearly 13 million of the 33.2 million U.S. small businesses are women-owned, yet female entrepreneurs receive only 16% of first-round venture funding. To bridge this funding gap, various private and federal grants and resources are available for women-owned businesses. Key private grants include the Amber Grant, IFundWomen, Women Founders Network Fast Pitch Competition, and others such as the HerRise MicroGrant, FoundHer Program, and High Five Grant for Moms. Federal options include Grants.gov, SBIR/STTR programs, and the PRIME initiative. Additional resources like DreamBuilder, the Office of Women’s Business Ownership, and Belle Capital USA offer training, mentorship, and funding. Professional organizations such as the National Women’s Business Council help influence policy and support women in business. To qualify for many grants, a business must be at least 51% woman-owned. Certification as a Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) can enhance access to federal resources. A strong grant proposal should clearly align with the grantor's mission, with valid documentation and a defined use plan. For military spouses and others, the Small Business Administration offers targeted support. These resources collectively aim to empower and support the growth of women-led businesses across various industries.

### Tell us about your business or business idea…

The Luxora Collective was born out of one of the hardest seasons of my life. After experiencing years of emotional and physical abuse, I found myself rebuilding from the ground up, personally, financially, and professionally. What could have broken me instead became the foundation for something much bigger than myself.

For over 12 years, I worked inside the medical aesthetics industry, starting from the front desk and eventually managing multiple med spa locations. I saw firsthand how many talented women entered this industry with incredible passion and skill, only to become overwhelmed by the business side of things. Many of them were carrying the weight of families, employees, financial pressure, and the constant demand to “do it all.” I understood that pressure deeply because I had lived it myself.

I started The Luxora Collective to help women in aesthetics build businesses that are not only profitable, but sustainable, empowering, and aligned with the life they actually want to live. We help med spa and wellness owners identify “revenue leaks,” improve client experience, increase retention, and build systems that allow them to grow without burning themselves out.

What motivates me most is helping women realize they are capable of more than survival. I want them to build wealth, confidence, leadership skills, and freedom through businesses they are proud of. There is something incredibly powerful about watching another woman finally feel in control of her future again.

The opportunity in this industry is enormous. Medical aesthetics and wellness continue to grow rapidly, but many small business owners are underserved when it comes to mentorship, operational guidance, and sustainable growth systems. My experience gives me a unique ability to bridge the gap between strategy and real-world operations because I have lived every level of it myself.

The biggest challenge has been scaling while rebuilding my own life at the same time. I launched this company during a period of personal transition and recovery, while also continuing to support my family and team. But despite those challenges, the business has continued to grow because it is rooted in authenticity, experience, and genuine passion for helping others succeed.

The Luxora Collective represents resilience, second chances, and the belief that women can rise from incredibly difficult circumstances and create something meaningful, impactful, and lasting.


---

### Tell us what you would do with the money if awarded a grant…

If awarded this grant, I would use the funding to expand The Luxora Collective and invest directly into building opportunities for other young women who want to learn business, leadership, marketing, and entrepreneurship.

Right now, we are a small but mighty team of four. Every single person on my team plays a huge role in helping our clients succeed, but we are reaching the point where demand is growing faster than our current capacity. This funding would allow us to hire and train additional women who are eager to grow professionally and build meaningful careers within our company.

One of my greatest passions is mentorship. I know what it feels like to start over with limited resources and simply need someone to believe in you and teach you the skills you were never given access to before. I want to create a company where women can learn not only how to market and grow businesses, but also how to lead, communicate confidently, build systems, manage clients, and create financial independence for themselves.

The grant would also help us strengthen the systems and infrastructure needed to scale responsibly, including technology, client delivery systems, education resources, and team development. This would allow us to serve more women-owned med spas and wellness businesses across the country while maintaining the personalized support and relationship-driven approach we are known for.

Most importantly, this funding would create a ripple effect. By helping us grow, you are also helping the many female business owners we support every day, women who are trying to build successful businesses while balancing families, employees, financial pressure, and personal growth.

This business started from resilience and survival, but my vision for it is much bigger than me. I want to build a company that creates opportunity, confidence, mentorship, and long-term impact for women for years to come.
